title: Specialization respects normalized Hom coordinates and their addition
statement:
Fix a finite-field datum $D=(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-numbers, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and any scheme $Y$ with no structure map to $k$; its universe is independent of that of $\Omega$. Let $I$ be the directed finite coefficient subfields [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set]. On the fixed intrinsic rational stages $C_E=\mathrm{sfRationalConstructibleCategory}(\ell,\mathrm{Shrink}(E),Y)$, obtained by raw rationalization of the intrinsic integral category [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed, def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], let $S$ and $S_D$ be the normalized scalar systems with proof parameters $0$ and $p$, respectively [lem-general-algebraically-closed-coefficient-stages]. Use the equality $\eta:S=S_D$ of [lem-pur-general-specialization-pairs], and set $P=S.\mathrm{PairCategory}$, $P_D=S_D.\mathrm{PairCategory}$ [def-sf-directed-common-stage-data]. Let $e:P\simeq P_D$ be equality transport, namely $\mathrm{Pi.eqToEquivalence}(T\mapsto T.\mathrm{PairCategory},\eta)$; this specifies the functor, not an arbitrary equivalence.

Use the pair and transport identifications of [lem-pur-general-specialization-pairs], the prescribed colimit Hom groups on $P$ [lem-pur-general-pair-hom-coordinates], and those on $P_D$ [lem-pur-general-intrinsic-finite-field-transport]. Let $c_{A,B}$ and $c^D_{eA,eB}$ be their unique representative-normalized coordinate equivalences [def-weil-directed-colimit-abelian-groups]. For every $f:A\to B$,
$$c^D_{eA,eB}(e(f))=c_{A,B}(f)$$
after the equality identification of the colimit families induced by $\eta$. Moreover $e$ preserves the prescribed zero morphisms and sums: $e(0)=0$ and $e(f+g)=e(f)+e(g)$ for all parallel arrows. This is additivity for the already prescribed preadditive structures [def-weil-preadditive-category], not a new structure transported to make the assertion true.

source.note: Construction material from old argument 10 (retained verbatim): For specialization_additive, use that specialization is an equivalence. It preserves the zero object and binary products, which exist in the pretriangulated source. A private abstract equivalence lemma first supplies preservation of zero morphisms from preservation of the initial object, then applies Mathlib Functor.additive_of_preserves_binary_products. Specializing it proves additivity for the already prescribed preadditive structures. The explicit zero-morphism step is as follows. The equivalence preserves the zero object because its inverse transports each unique arrow, so a zero morphism, factored through a zero object, maps to zero. It preserves binary products by the same transport of their universal property. These products exist in the pretriangulated source. Apply lem-sfb-products-zero-additive (Mathlib Functor.additive_of_preserves_binary_products) with these fixed group structures. For the coordinate clause, on [L,u] both specifications give the image of u under the same colimit structure map: specialization_pairs keeps its label and finite map, and specialization_transport identifies the transition maps. Every arrow has a finite representative, so representative induction gives equality on all arrows. This retains the additional normalization argument from the former supporting proof, not just its additive conclusion.

proof.text: Use $\eta$ and the transport clause of [lem-pur-general-specialization-pairs] to identify, for fixed $A,B$, the finite Hom groups and every transition map of the two systems. Equality transport identifies their abelian-group colimits and their canonical homomorphisms $\iota_L$ [def-weil-directed-colimit-abelian-groups]: after eliminating the equality of systems, this identification is the identity. In particular it preserves zero and addition and takes each $\iota_L(u)$ to the same class. Denote this identification by $J$.

proof.text: Given $f:A\to B$, choose a finite representative $f=[L,u]$ using [lem-pur-general-pair-hom-coordinates]. The pair clause of [lem-pur-general-specialization-pairs] gives $e(f)=[L,u_D]$, where $u_D$ is the equality transport of $u$. The prescribed coordinate formulas of [lem-pur-general-pair-hom-coordinates] and [lem-pur-general-intrinsic-finite-field-transport] now give $c^D(e(f))=\iota^D_L(u_D)=J(\iota_L(u))=J(c(f))$. The representative exists for every arrow, so this proves the claimed coordinate identity for all $f$.

proof.text: The prescribed Hom groups in [lem-pur-general-pair-hom-coordinates] and [lem-pur-general-intrinsic-finite-field-transport] are transferred from their colimits by $c$ and $c^D$, respectively. Thus these coordinate equivalences preserve zero and addition for those already fixed laws. Applying step 2 to zero gives $c^D(e(0))=J(c(0))=0=c^D(0)$. For parallel $f,g$, it gives $c^D(e(f+g))=J(c(f+g))=J(c(f))+J(c(g))=c^D(e(f))+c^D(e(g))=c^D(e(f)+e(g))$. Injectivity of $c^D$ proves $e(0)=0$ and $e(f+g)=e(f)+e(g)$. No Hom group structure is replaced in this argument.

lean.statement:
theorem specialization_homCoordinates (A B : Pair l Ω Y) (f : A ⟶ B) :
    HEq
      (SfAlgebraicallyClosedCoefficients.homCoordinates
        ((specialization D l hl Ω Y).functor.obj A)
        ((specialization D l hl Ω Y).functor.obj B)
        ((specialization D l hl Ω Y).functor.map f))
      (homCoordinates A B f)
lean.note: Existing statements cover both clauses for the specified Pi.eqToEquivalence specialization: specialization_homCoordinates gives equality of the normalized colimit coordinates after system equality identification (HEq); specialization_additive is additivity for the already prescribed preadditive structures. The zero formula follows directly from the standard Functor.preservesZeroMorphisms_of_additive instance and Functor.map_zero, without changing either Hom group law. No new module, statement correction or proof completion.
